notes: Settings → More is one list of rows now, the way a phone's settings should read: the title on the left, what it is doing on the right, and a marker that turns as the row opens. Tap a row and its controls slide out under it — nothing is on the screen that you did not ask for.

Nothing was left out. Every setting that used to sit loose between two cards is a row of its own: the tutorial, the Playlists / Albums button, auto-scroll to song, keep the playing album open, ask artist when importing, and About — whose version number is now on its row with the update log, the listening streak and the version guide inside it.

Playback and Playback & sound are one thing. Two menus over the same subject are one menu: crossfade, seek style, auto-volume, the assistant duck, the sleep timer, gapless, the next-album roll, the per-playlist sort, the 8-band equalizer, the volume boost and the anti-muffler all live in Playback & sound, in four labelled parts.

An anti-muffler sits right under the volume boost. A boxed-in master is usually a build-up around 320 Hz and a roll-off above a few kilohertz, so this cuts the first by 3.5 dB and lifts the second by 3.5 dB — the same size on purpose, because an uneven pair is a preset and this is not one. It colours whatever is playing, on top of your own equalizer.

The anti-muffler comes back on the next launch and applies to a song that is already playing, with no restart and no press of play. Off is exactly how SideCut sounded before this release — the signal is multiplied by 1 and a zero is added to it, and nothing in the audio graph is ever disconnected to switch it, so there is no click and no gap.

The drop-down slides open instead of appearing, and it opens to whatever it is holding — the storage numbers and the DJ Mode list can still change height while they are open. Reduce motion (Sandbox) keeps the instant flip, and so does any device that will not report a height.
